page: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is built on the x86_64 architecture and includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is network-based with a capacity of 1 GB, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this hardware configuration.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier. However, multi-core performance scales moderately, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores falling into the average category. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a notable bottleneck, registering in the bottom 25% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth and database operations, including Redis SET operations at 8.04 million operations per second, consistently perform within the average range.

The server exhibits a clear tradeoff between high single-threaded efficiency and moderate multi-threaded scaling, likely due to its 2 physical cores hosting 4 virtual threads. While it handles small-model LLM inference and text processing efficiently, prompt processing for medium-sized 7B models is poor, placing in the bottom 10%. Given the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and network-attached storage, this instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, single-threaded applications, lightweight web serving, and basic database operations rather than highly parallelized compute-intensive tasks or large-scale local storage processing.
